questions.question: What is the difference between mutable and immutable objects in Python?
questions.title: Mutable vs Immutable Objects in Python
questions.direct_answer: Mutable objects can change in place, such as list, dict, and set. Immutable objects cannot change after creation, such as int, float, bool, str, tuple, and frozenset; an apparent change creates a new object. Variables are names bound to objects, not typed boxes.

sections.content:
Mutable objects can change in place, such as list, dict, and set.

Python variables hold references to objects. A mutable object can be updated without changing its identity; an immutable value must be replaced.

A common mistake is calling a variable itself mutable or assuming tuple contents are always deeply immutable.

```python
b = a
a.append(3)   # b sees [1, 2, 3]

y = x

```
